title: Abraham Lincoln and Grace Bedell: An 11-Year-Old Girl's Advice on Growing a Beard (1860)
summary: In October 1860, 11-year-old Grace Bedell wrote to presidential candidate Abraham Lincoln advising him to grow whiskers. Lincoln’s warm reply and subsequent meeting reveal his profound humility.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 144: ஆபிரகாம் லிங்கனும் கிரேஸ் பெடலும்: தாடி வளர்க்கலாமா?
full_text:
In October 1860, during the fiercely contested United States presidential campaign, candidate Abraham Lincoln was clean-shaven, his tall, gaunt frame and deeply lined face frequently lampooned by political cartoonists.

In Westfield, New York, an eleven-year-old girl named Grace Bedell saw Lincoln's campaign portrait and decided to write him a candid letter:
"Hon. A. B. Lincoln,
My father has just come home from the fair and brought home your picture. I want that you should not think me bold to write to such a great man as you are. Have you any little girls? If you have not any, I have got four brothers and part of them will vote for you anyway, and if you let your whiskers grow I will try and get the rest of them to vote for you. You would look a great deal better for your face is so thin. All the ladies like whiskers and they would tease their husbands to vote for you and then you would be President."

Amidst the avalanche of national correspondence, Lincoln personally penned a gentle, humorous reply on October 19:
"My dear little Miss,
Your very agreeable letter of the 15th is received. As to the whiskers, having never worn any, do you not think people would call it a piece of silly affectation if I were to begin it now? Your very sincere well-wisher, A. Lincoln."

Yet Lincoln took her advice to heart. By the time his inaugural train rolled toward Washington in February 1861, he had grown the iconic full beard that defined his presidency. When the train stopped at Westfield, Lincoln stepped onto the platform and called out for Grace Bedell. Kneeling before the astonished young girl, he kissed her cheek and said, "You see, Grace, I let these whiskers grow for you."

The episode remains a timeless testament to Lincoln's unaffected warmth and capacity to listen to everyday citizens.
